question: Does option 1 clear the floor and the proposed bar on ALL 420 pre-cutover days, and is the worst day the same one the 24-day projection named?
denominator_is_fixed_because: star_rows_already_complete == 0 and every STAR valid-label row already carries the seven non-industry dense factors, so the STAR rows are inside V today and a backfill moves only N

projected_full_window_g6.note: pre-cutover 420 days measured here under the conservative bound; post-cutover 549 days taken from the instrument, whose coverage already exceeds 0.971 and whose SH/SZ-union perturbation was measured at a median relative difference of 0.0 (problems_found.md §X-续三)

answer: YES on the floor, and the 24-day projection's worst day survives the full census unchanged. Over all 420 pre-cutover days the backfill takes days below 0.9 from 24 to 0, and the minimum coverage after the fix is 0.9490312966 on 2022-07-29 -- digit-for-digit the day and value the 24-day projection reported, 4 rows short of the proposed 0.95 bar. The worst of the 396 days that never broke the floor is 0.973924, so the assertion 'the other days can only improve' is now measured rather than assumed. Against the 0.95 bar exactly one day of 420 fails. Projected full-window G6 is 969/969 = 1.000000 at the floor (currently 945/969 = 0.975232) and 968/969 = 0.998968 at the bar.
